task: Revise the Drink Stand minigame in esl-likes: adopt the shared speech-focus service clock so every window's pressure pauses while the child speaks, replace press-and-wait pouring with one forgiving hold-to-fill mechanic across all six stations, give each station its own look and sound without changing its controls, and reduce the customer counts.
notes: READ FIRST, in this order: SPEC.md section 3 subsection 'Protected speech focus', SPEC.md section 6 (the whole Drink Stand section — its Controls and Difficulty subsections were rewritten today and are the frozen design you are implementing), then the four 2026-09-12 entries at the end of DESIGN_DECISIONS.md. Those documents are the contract. Where this brief and SPEC disagree, SPEC wins and you should say so in your summary.

CONTEXT. esl-likes is a 3D ESL game for Japanese Grade 3 children on classroom Chromebooks. The child asks 'What drink do you like?', the NPC answers 'I like orange juice.', and the child must find that station among six shuffled ones, make the drink and serve it. The frozen rules are that the NPC's answer must be information the child genuinely needs, and that recognition noise is the game's problem and never the child's.

DRINK STAND IS NOT BEING REDESIGNED. Its comprehension structure is already the strongest in the project — keep it. It is the fastest, most arcade minigame: hear, identify the machine, make, serve. It is spoken English to recognition to written/visual English to physical action; it is NOT a person-order memory game, which is what the Restaurant (redesigned in a separate, already completed order) is for. Do not make the two converge.

ALREADY DONE FOR YOU — do not rebuild or modify these. (1) src/systems/speechFocus.js exists, is tested and is frozen: `createSpeechFocus({ floor = 0, enterDuration = 0.12, releaseDuration = 0.35 })` returns `{ begin(reason), end(), cancel(), update(dt), serviceDelta(dt), get active, get scale }`. scale is 1 in normal play, ramps to the floor while focused, ramps back to exactly 1 after end(). begin() is idempotent; cancel() snaps back for minigame exit. (2) All new Japanese UI strings already exist in src/config/lesson.js under UI.drinkStand: `pourHint` (now names the hold), `pourDrink`, `topUp`, `fullCup`, `overflow`, alongside the existing `pouring` and `poured`. Use these; do NOT edit src/config/lesson.js, because a parallel order is forbidden from touching it too and any edit there will conflict.

PROBLEM ONE — SPEECH PROTECTION IS CURRENTLY WRONG, and this is the most important fix in this order. updateCustomers contains `if (questionCustomer !== customer) customer.patience = Math.max(0, customer.patience - dt)`. That pauses only the customer being spoken to, so on Normal and Challenge the OTHER one or two window customers keep draining while the child is speaking — the game punishes a child for speaking English, in a game about speaking English. Worse, a child whose sentence needed two recognition attempts pays twice. Remove that per-timer guard entirely and replace it with the structural fix below.

THE SERVICE CLOCK. Keep `elapsed` for cosmetic animation (stream wobble, fizz, billboarding) and add `serviceElapsed` advanced by `focus.serviceDelta(safeDt)`. EVERY pressure clock must read the service delta or serviceElapsed, never raw dt: customer arrival scheduling (`spawnAt`, and note `rushStart` is computed from the arrival schedule), ALL window patience, queue promotion, the rush schedule, and the fill/pour progress. Call `focus.update(safeDt)` once per frame with the real dt. The point of the structure is that the next timer added to this file freezes correctly by default rather than needing its own guard. Focus lifecycle: `focus.begin()` when the talk prompt opens (today: targetQuestion), `focus.end()` when it resolves or is abandoned (today: acceptQuestion and clearQuestion), `focus.begin()` for the final turnaround prompt, `focus.cancel()` in exit(). Focus must cover holding the button, recognition running, the judging pause, a RETRY after failed recognition, and the mic-free read-and-tap fallback. The acceptance test is that a sentence needing two attempts costs no more service time than one that worked first try, and that the ラッシュ！ finale freezes with everything else — a child must never hurry their English because the rush is on. Optional cheap polish: duck the ambient audio while focused. Do NOT move the camera and do NOT add postprocessing.

PROBLEM TWO — POURING IS FLAVOURLESS. It is currently `startPour` sets `pourRemaining = POUR_SECONDS` (1s) and `finishPour` hands over a full cup. Replace it with ONE hold-to-fill mechanic, identical at all six stations: press and hold Space at a station, the dispenser runs, liquid visibly rises in the cup mesh, release to stop. Six stations, NOT six minigames — the control must be identical everywhere, only the look and sound differ.

FILL FORGIVENESS — the exact rule, and note what is deliberately NOT included. A cup at or above roughly 35% is already a valid, servable drink. Below that it is visibly underfilled and can be topped up by holding again AT THE SAME STATION (use UI.drinkStand.topUp); starting a DIFFERENT drink still empties the cup first, as today. Reaching full is the best visual feedback (UI.drinkStand.fullCup). Holding past full plays a comic overflow/fizz/spill and the drink REMAINS VALID (UI.drinkStand.overflow). Fill level must NEVER enter the score in any form: no fill-quality term, not even a tiny efficiency component. That was explicitly considered and rejected, because it creates a pouring-skill axis competing with listening and a Grade 3 child cannot tell why their stars dropped. A correct drink must never be discarded or downgraded for holding the button slightly too long. Listening stays more important than pouring, always.

THE TRACKPAD ROUTE MATTERS — get this right or the mouse-only child is penalised relative to the keyboard child. Clicking/tapping a station must still auto-walk there as it does today. Once at a station the on-screen action control must be holdable (pointerdown starts filling, pointerup stops) rather than a plain click. Crucially, a SHORT TAP — press and release inside roughly 150ms, which is what a trackpad tap actually produces — must latch the dispenser and fill to full on its own rather than producing a useless dribble. A real hold behaves as a hold. Every input route must end in a valid cup. Also note the keyboard interaction with the speech system: src/systems/speech.js HoldToTalk captures Space globally on keydown/keyup with stopImmediatePropagation while a talk prompt is enabled, so hold-Space-to-fill is only safe while no prompt is open. Verify there is no conflict where a prompt and a station overlap, and make sure releasing Space after a talk prompt closes cannot accidentally start a fill.

STATION PERSONALITY — visual and audio only, never control changes. Water: pale blue transparent stream, clean splash. Milk: thick white stream, softer pour. Orange juice: bright orange stream. Apple juice: pale gold. Tea: amber with a small steam wisp. Soda: green melon-style with bubbles/fizz and a livelier dispensing sound. Use the existing audio system's sfx approach — do not add audio files or dependencies. Keep every station clearly distinguishable and keep its English word plainly readable at 1366x768; the written English word is part of the pedagogy. Effects must stay lightweight: no large particle systems, no postprocessing, no per-frame allocations in the update loop.

CUSTOMER COUNTS. Change DIFFICULTY from count 6/7/8 to 5/5/5-or-6 (choose 6 for level 3 if the rush still reads well with 6, otherwise 5 — say which you chose and why). Max simultaneous windows stays 1/2/3. Patience stays generous at all levels and forgiving at level 3. Asking one question eight times is repetition, not practice; five askings plus the turnaround is the target. Check that the rush still works after the count change — `rushStart` is derived as `(configured.count - 3) * 3.5` and the last three customers are the rush, so with 5 customers the rush is a larger share of the session; make sure the pacing still feels like a finale rather than the whole game.

KEEP ALL OF THIS WORKING: the six drinks and their station signs, station order shuffled once per session, each customer's drink chosen independently and uniformly with repeats allowed and nothing removed from the pool, no customer visual cue and no persistent order icon, empty hands at start, the queue where waiting customers have NO patience countdown until they occupy a window, the ラッシュ！ banner as a finale and never a fail state, the combo for consecutive first-try serves, wrong-drink behaviour (politely declines in Japanese, English NOT repeated, cup empties, first-try credit lost, combo resets), 🔊 もういちど きく forfeiting only the memory bonus, the turnaround accepting any of the six drinks, the click/tap-to-walk route, the existing debug hook window.__eslDebug.drinkStand, the finish() payload shape, and full resource disposal in exit including the focus cancel.

SCORING MODULE. src/minigames/drinkStand/scoring.js is pure and already tested — keep it that way. Do not add a fill-quality term to it. If the hold-to-fill state machine has logic worth testing (threshold for valid, top-up allowed, overflow still valid, switching drinks empties), extract it as a small pure module such as src/minigames/drinkStand/fill.js with its own .test.mjs in the house style (node:test + node:assert/strict), rather than burying it in three.js scene code where no test can reach it. Cover at least: an empty cup is not servable; filling past the valid threshold makes it servable; a partial cup tops up at the same station; a different drink empties it; holding past full leaves it valid and flags overflow; and fill level produces no scoring effect.

PLAYTHROUGH. Update scripts/playthrough-drink.mjs for the revised mechanics — the hold-to-fill interaction and the new customer counts will break the current click-to-pour driving. Keep both existing sessions: the listening route expecting three stars, and the anti-shortcut route that ignores answers and tries stations in a fixed order, which must NOT reach three stars. Add checks that all window patience is frozen while a prompt is open, that an underfilled cup can be topped up, that an overfilled cup still serves successfully, and that the revised counts and window limits are in effect. Extend the debug snapshot if the playthrough needs new fields (for example fill level, per-customer patience, and whether focus is active).

BEHAVIOURAL ACCEPTANCE IS REQUIRED — this is gameplay and visual work, so passing tests are not evidence that it plays correctly. Run the real thing and look at it: `npm run build`, then `npm run playthrough:drink-stand` (the project runner starts and always stops its own preview server, runs scripts/playthrough-drink.mjs, and writes screenshots plus a manifest.json under .tmp/playthrough/drink-stand/). Never start a raw `vite preview` yourself. Keep the playthrough at viewport 1366x768, the real classroom Chromebook resolution. Capture screenshots of: all six stations with their signs readable, a cup part-filled, a cup full, an overflow, the stand with 2-3 active windows, the ラッシュ！ banner, the combo pop, and the turnaround. Report what you actually observed on the result's `behavioralValidation` field with `performed`, `observed: true` ONLY if you really looked at rendered output, `method`, `viewport: '1366x768'`, `checks` and `passed`. Saying it looks right without having looked is a claim, not an observation. Specifically confirm by looking: the six machines are distinguishable at a glance, the English labels are readable, the liquid level in the cup is obvious, the overflow reads as playful rather than as an error, the windows stay readable with three customers present, and ラッシュ！ does not cover information the child needs.

If your own new Playwright checks fail, remember the harness is materially changed and therefore untrusted: verify the locator, viewport and scene state before concluding the game is broken. Inspect the screenshot or DOM first.

Append a short DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entry ONLY if you make a design decision this brief and SPEC do not already cover — for example your level-3 customer count choice if you deviate. The four entries for today's redesign are already written; do not duplicate or rewrite them, and do not edit SPEC.md.
requirements: The per-customer patience guard is gone and a service clock drives every pressure timer — arrivals, all window patience, queue promotion, the rush schedule and fill progress — via focus.serviceDelta, while cosmetic animation keeps raw frame dt; focus.update runs once per frame and focus.cancel runs in exit

While a talk prompt is open — including a retry after failed recognition and the mic-free fallback — EVERY active window's patience is frozen, no customer arrives or is promoted from the queue, the rush does not advance, and fill progress does not advance
A sentence needing two recognition attempts consumes no more service time than one accepted on the first attempt
All six stations use one identical hold-to-fill control: holding runs the dispenser, liquid visibly rises in the cup, releasing stops it

A cup at or above the valid threshold is servable; an underfilled cup can be topped up at the same station; starting a different drink empties the cup; holding past full plays an overflow effect and the drink remains valid and servable
Fill level has no effect on the score in any form, and no fill-quality term is added to the scoring module
A short tap of the on-screen action latches the fill and reaches full on its own, so the trackpad-only route always ends in a valid cup, while a real hold behaves as a hold
Holding Space to fill does not conflict with the speech system's global Space capture, and closing a talk prompt cannot accidentally start a fill
Each station is visually and audibly distinct with its English word readable at 1366x768, using the existing audio system and no new assets or dependencies
Customer counts are 5 / 5 / 5-or-6 with max windows 1 / 2 / 3, patience generous throughout, and the rush still reads as a finale
Station order still shuffles per session, each customer's drink is still independent and uniform with repeats allowed, no customer cue or persistent order icon exists, and hands start empty
Queued customers still have no patience countdown until they occupy a window
Wrong-drink behaviour is unchanged: polite Japanese refusal, English not repeated, cup empties, first-try credit lost, combo resets
The combo, Listen Again memory-bonus semantics, ラッシュ！ finale, turnaround accepting any of the six drinks, click-to-walk route, finish payload shape and full disposal all still work

If a fill state machine module is extracted it is pure with no DOM or three.js, and its .test.mjs covers the valid threshold, top-up, drink switching, overflow validity and the absence of any scoring effect

scripts/playthrough-drink.mjs is updated for hold-to-fill and the new counts, keeps its listening and anti-shortcut sessions with the same star expectations, and adds checks for frozen patience during a prompt, top-up, and a successful overfilled serve
npm test passes including the pre-existing 147 tests, npm run build is clean, and the Drink Stand playthrough passes at 1366x768

behavioralValidation is reported from rendered output actually observed, with screenshots covering the six stations, a part-filled cup, a full cup, an overflow, multiple active windows, the rush banner, the combo and the turnaround
constraints: Do NOT modify src/config/lesson.js — every string you need was added there already, and a parallel order is also forbidden from touching it; editing it will cause a conflict
Do NOT modify src/systems/speechFocus.js or its test — that module is frozen and already reviewed

Do NOT modify src/minigames/restaurant/** or scripts/playthrough.mjs — Claude may be editing those files while you work. Read them for patterns (the Restaurant already uses speechFocus and a service clock, and has a combo pop and debug hook), never edit them
Do NOT modify scripts/playthrough-run.mjs or package.json scripts; use `npm run playthrough:drink-stand` as it is
Do NOT modify SPEC.md, and do not rewrite the existing 2026-09-12 DESIGN_DECISIONS.md entries

Do not modify the other minigames (coloring, sports, zoo) or the shared shell, HUD, dialogue, speech matcher, characters, progression or save systems; if you believe a shared file must change, stop and report instead
Do not turn Drink Stand into a memory game, do not add person-order tracking, and do not extract a shared service-game abstraction with the Restaurant — the two controllers are deliberately different
Do not create six different filling interactions, minigames or control schemes; the control is identical at every station
Do not move the camera during speech focus, add postprocessing, add large particle systems, add per-frame allocations in the update loop, or add any npm dependency
Edit files with your structured patch/edit tool. If a shell-based edit fails once because of quoting or escaping, switch to the structured mechanism — do not try another escaped variant
Do not commit, push, merge, rewrite git history, or revert the uncommitted SPEC.md, DESIGN_DECISIONS.md and lesson.js changes already in the working tree — those are the input to this task
